 When you are not confident on a football pitch, your automatic reaction is retreat, sit still and sort of let the game come onto you and see it. That doesn't work at the highest level and that's what they're suffering from.

 'Man Utd need to decide who will be in charge against Bournemouth' published at 23:01 BST 23:01 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter in Como 
 I think Michael Carrick is almost struggling for answers at the moment. 
 I don't know if it's the angriest he's been, I think he's been quite forceful in his pre-match press conferences with the media lately, I have been on the wrong end of that. He does it in quite a calm way, not like Sir Alex Ferguson but I think he's trying to be on the front foot and today is just a really bad day.
 I immediately thought when he went to the fans, acknowledging them like he did, hands in the air, four or five times, was a bit like Ole Gunnar Solskjær who did something very similar after a 4-1 defeat to Watford. He admitted that he knew at half-time in that game that his time at Manchester United would come to an end.
 Now, United have flown straight back after the game so presumably there will be a lot of thought going on on that plane as it heads back to Manchester. But, first of all, Manchester United need to decide who will be in charge of that game against Bournemouth on Sunday, and Bournemouth aren't in brilliant form, they won the last game, but they have only won one game this season, and they are playing tomorrow night so Manchester United should be really looking to win that game even though Bournemouth have a fantastic record at Old Trafford. 
 Do Manchester United give Michael Carrick that game and see from there, or do they think we need to make a change?

 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Stephen Warnock 
Former Liverpool defender on MOTD: UEFA Champions League 
 Manchester United didn't know how to press, when to press. The intensity just wasn't there so I totally understand what Michael Carrick is saying, if you don't run off the ball, forward and back, you're not going to get results. 
 I'm sure Manchester United fans are sat at home now saying 'what's next, where do we go from here?'.

 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United

Former Man City defender on MOTD: UEFA Champions League 
 For them [Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes] to be clashing with their messaging after such a tough defeat is a huge issue because you want everybody to sort of come together, try and figure out a way to get through difficult times on the same page but for those two it definitely doesn't seem to be the case.

 Have Man Utd lost their 'aura'? published at 22:55 BST 22:55 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Matt Upson 
Former Arsenal defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 There is a grace period you have, I think when you have been as great as what that club is. Time surpasses when it becomes normalised, you lose the aura of what Manchester United was. Whenever I played or pulled up at Old Trafford it was a very unpleasant experience on the feild and that was felt by many a player and a club over that period.
 It is now quite a good place to go and turn Manchester United over and that is becoming the norm so that's a dangerous thing for a club that had that kind of aura that won matches before a ball was kicked.

 'Overall we were better' published at 22:54 BST 22:54 BST 
 FT: Aston Villa 3-1 Viking 
 Aston Villa 
 Villa boss Unai Emery told TNT Sports: "We played a very safe match. 
 "First half we dominated. We were feeling comfortable. The second half we started not like the first half and conceded some corners. In 90 minutes overall we were better and dominated more than less.
 "We're so happy how we're getting those three points."

 'Manchester United are still Manchester United' published at 22:46 BST 22:46 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Kasper Schmeichel 
Former Celtic goalkeeper on 5 Live 
 Manchester United are still Manchester United, and Liverpool went through a similar phrase and it took a very long long time for them to get back. What it required was the right people.
 Brendan Rodgers came in and started to turn things around, obviously there was Rafa Benitez, but I'm talking particularly in the Premier League. He put some foundations in place and then Jurgen Klopp came in, and that's when they really accelerated and became the Liverpool that they are today.

 'Arsenal will miss Saka but have players who can step up' published at 22:42 BST 22:42 BST 
 FT: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal 
 Nedum Onuoha 
Former Man City defender on MOTD: UEFA Champions League 
 As far as the game goes, getting a result like that against Bayern, with Arsenal probably believing they could go on and get the win at the end, is very impressive.
 The only negative is seeing one of their star players, Saka, having to pull up with an injury early in the first half. He was lying on the floor with his hand up and he knew he was in a bit of trouble, so now the concern will be how long he is out for.
 (Saka's absence) It's not necessarily something that means the team will struggle heavily but there is a reason why he is regarded as one of the best players in this Arsenal team and is seen as being important for them. They will still be hoping he isn't out for so long.
 This is one of the reasons their squad has been built the way it has been and I think Madueke and Eze did well on the wings today after Saka came off (Madueke had started on the left but switched to the right with Eze coming on to the left).
 In terms of options, at this moment in time for Arsenal, it is not going to be an issue... they will miss the star power that he has, they still have plenty of other wide players who can step up and do the job while they wait for him to come back.

 It feels like 'open season' for Man Utd published at 22:33 BST 22:33 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Matt Upson 
Former Arsenal defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 What teams aren't in better shape and form than Manchester United? Manchester United for me get results because they spent a lot of money and they do have players that can do things, and they will win some football matches, but at the moment it's just open season it feels at the club.
 That's a very difficult thing to deal with, can you be successful on the pitch when that's going on? Probably not, I don't think that's possible. I wasn't surprised to see that they really struggled against a team that's on the complete opposite side of where they are. 
 [Como are] together, fresh, new, have something to prove and grabbing their opportunity as a group. 
 There is something definitely wrong, and to criticise not the manager directly, but the tactics, which land at his feet is so damaging.
 53 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A fascinating game' published at 22:31 BST 22:31 BST 
 FT: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, speaking to TNT Sports: "That is one of the highest levels we played. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game. 
 "We started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant. Then we had to adapt without Saka. In the second half the game was a bit even and they scored the goals and we had to react, which we did. We scored and we had the chance to win it too. That is the level."
 On Saka's injury: "They are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see."
